title: Post-standup action list + triage notes
body:
Context:
- Quick post-standup capture. Hit a reproducible p99 spike on frontend route /v1/generate yesterday evening; appears correlated with KV cache churn when sequence lengths jump (long prompts + user messages).
- Customer report: intermittent tail latency increases (15% of requests) during mixed short+long sequences. No token-level errors, just timeouts at API gateway when backend took >3s.
- Current hypothesis: aggressive per-session KV cache eviction + microbatch scheduler failing to coalesce across large seq-length variance -> some requests starved behind long decode.

Immediate reproducer (local):
1) Checkout branch: runtime/eviction-play-1428
   - GH PR above has a regression patch candidate.
2) Run reproducer script: tools/reproducers/kv-evict-mix.sh --seed 42 --clients 16 --seq-dist "short:0.7,long:0.3"
3) Use monitor: scripts/trace-tail-latency.sh --filter route=/v1/generate --top 100
4) Observe: KV cache eviction spikes around t+30s, p99 jumps to 1.8x baseline.

Notes-to-self from running repro (11:30am):
- Eviction metric 'kv_evicted_keys' increments in spikes rather than smooth low-level churn. Looks like an eviction batch triggered by memory pressure threshold oscillation.
- microbatcher logs show batch size collapse (from 8 to 1) when long requests inserted; decode loop holds GPU longer -> backlog -> scheduler fallback path introduces extra latency.
- On a 4-GPU dedicated node, the effect is visible but amplified when node has other tenants (context switching for kernel streams).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Eviction threshold hysteresis: threshold calculation uses instantaneous memory usage; short bursts push eviction and then usage drops, but eviction continues until next GC window. Fix: add hysteresis / min-interval between evictions.
2) Microbatch scheduler not weight-normalizing by expected decode time; it currently weights by arrival time only. Fix: introduce cost-estimate per request (seq_len * model_factor) for batch forming.
3) KV cache representation uses a global LRU that is O(n) expensive during eviction cycles for high-concurrency sessions. Consider moving to segmented LRU or time-windowed buckets.

Immediate action items (owner / ETA):
- A: Add a short-term guard to prevent eviction storms (throttle evictions to max X keys per second). Owner: Maya. ETA: EOD today.
- B: Prototype request-cost estimation in microbatch scheduler (heuristic: seq_len * 0.7 + prompt_len * 0.3). Owner: Evan. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
- C: Add logging around eviction decision path (include memory_before, memory_after, trigger_cause). Owner: Ravi. ETA: EOD today.
- D: Run smoke test on dedicated node with multi-tenant load after A/B. Owner: Marco (SRE). ETA: Tue 2026-03-17.

Short experiments to run (quick wins):
- Experiment 1: Increase eviction cooldown to 5s, run reproducer for 30 minutes. Metric: number of eviction bursts/min and p99 latency.
- Experiment 2: Limit microbatcher max-wait to 10ms to prefer larger batches when possible; see throughput vs latency tradeoff.
- Experiment 3: Run with KV cache disabled for sessions matching >80 token prompts to confirm cache is causal.

Quick commands / snippets I ran:
- Run repro (local): ./tools/reproducers/kv-evict-mix.sh --seed 42 --clients 16 --seq-dist "short:0.7,long:0.3" > /tmp/evict-run.log 2>&1 &
- Tail microbatcher: ssh node-42 "sudo journalctl -u runtime-microbatch -f --since '5m' | grep -i batch_size"
- Eviction metrics: curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_evicted_keys

Observations to log in GH PR:
- PR #1428 mitigates one eviction path but doesn't account for scheduler collapse. Leaving a detailed note in PR and linking this doc.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: If we add cost-estimation, should it be model-specific (per architecture) or generic? Tradeoffs: model-specific is more accurate but needs model-profile table.
- Q2: Do we prefer temporary throttle guards (fast to ship) or deeper LRU redesign (longer but robust)?
- Q3: Are there any SLA customers on node-42 to coordinate testing windows (ask SRE / customer success)?

Follow-ups for tomorrow:
- Walkthrough with Maya and Ravi 10:30am: go over logs and try A/B.
- If experiment 1 shows >50% reduction in eviction bursts, push guard patch to canary.
- Start a short doc outlining microbatch scheduler cost model (first pass in this doc, expand later).

Scratch ideas (not for immediate shipping):
- Instead of single global KV LRU, maintain per-session buckets and a global aging sampler that probabilistically evicts from heavy sessions. Might reduce big swings.
- Use adaptive batch windows driven by real-time estimate of decode_time instead of fixed timers.

Personal todo (low priority):
- Clean up repro scripts and add README.
- Add a per-request trace id in microbatch logs (helps correlate).

Random notes / brain dump:
- Saw an odd log: "kernel-stream-ctx-switch: 0x7ffb lost sync" — check driver/kernel logs later. Could be CUDA stream preemption in heavy decode.
- Remember to check NVLink bandwidth counters when we repro on multi-GPU node.

End of capture. Will iterate and move to a proper PR + Confluence summary if experiments are promising.

-- Evan
summary: Personal post-standup scratchpad capturing an investigation into p99 spikes correlated with KV cache eviction and microbatch scheduler collapse. Contains reproducer steps, hypotheses, immediate owners and ETAs, experiments, commands used, open questions, and follow-ups.
